questions.stem: According to the passage, what percentage of the world's population breathes air that does not meet WHO pollution guidelines at some point?
questions.evidence: about 99 percent of the world’s population breathes air at some point that does not meet pollution guidelines set by the World Health Organization (WHO)
questions.explanation_ko: 본문에 세계 인구의 약 99퍼센트가 WHO 오염 기준을 충족하지 못하는 공기를 마신다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT listed as a source of PM 10 particles?
questions.evidence: Larger particles, known as PM 10, are linked to agriculture, roadways, mining or wind-blown dust.
questions.explanation_ko: PM10 입자는 농업, 도로, 채굴, 바람에 날리는 먼지와 관련이 있다고 나와 있지만 해류는 언급되지 않았습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the passage about people who work outdoors for a living?
options: They are less likely to be affected by air pollution than people who work indoors.
They often cannot follow the advice to stay indoors during periods of bad air quality.
They are required by law to wear masks in polluted cities.
They tend to live in cities with the lowest air quality index numbers.
questions.evidence: there are many people who live or work outside and “can’t really afford ” to stay indoors
questions.explanation_ko: 실외에서 일하는 사람들은 실내에 머물 여유가 없다고 언급되어 그 조언을 따르기 어렵다는 것을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author include the quote from Rajasekhar Balasubramanian about a tiny air purifier in a large room?
options: To argue that air purifiers should never be used indoors
To illustrate a limitation of air purifiers in large spaces
To compare air purifier brands available in stores
To explain how air purifiers are manufactured
questions.evidence: If we have a tiny air purifier in a large room, it won’t be effective.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 인용문은 공기청정기가 큰 공간에서는 효과가 떨어질 수 있다는 한계를 보여 주기 위해 쓰였습니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "guidelines" mean as used in "pollution guidelines set by the World Health Organization"?
questions.evidence: pollution guidelines set by the World Health Organization (WHO)
questions.explanation_ko: 여기서 guidelines는 WHO가 정한 공식 권장 기준을 의미합니다.

blanks.sentence_ko: 그는 AP에 실외에서 살거나 일하는 사람이 많아 실내에 머물 여유가 없다고 말했다.
이 장치는 방 안의 공기를 빨아들인 뒤 오염물질을 가두는 필터를 통과시켜 작동한다.
전문가들은 대기질이 나쁠 때는 실내에 머물거나 마스크를 써서 노출을 제한하는 것이 목표가 되어야 한다고 말한다.
큰 방에 작은 공기청정기를 두면 효과가 없을 것이다.
모든 숨이 중요하지만 너무 많은 아이들에게는 숨 쉬는 것 자체가 해를 끼칠 수 있다.

key_points: About 99 percent of the world's population breathes air that fails WHO pollution guidelines, and air pollution kills about 7 million people a year.
Air can be dangerous even when it looks clear, and pollution comes from sources like burning fuel, agriculture, wildfires, and household activities such as cooking.
Short-term exposure can trigger asthma attacks, heart attacks, and strokes, while long-term exposure can cause fatal heart and lung disease; children are especially vulnerable.
Air quality indexes and monitoring apps help people track pollution levels, but not everyone can avoid exposure by staying indoors.
Air purifiers can reduce indoor pollution but work well mainly in small spaces with few people nearby.
main_idea: Air pollution is a serious and widespread health risk, and while there are ways to reduce personal exposure, they are not equally available or effective for everyone.
restate_sentence: Short-term exposure can cause asthma attacks and increase the risk of heart attacks and stroke, especially in older people and those with existing medical problems.
